I. PART I : NHGIS and the US county population

1. Extraction and Preprocessing

In this section, we define our API, then proceed with data extraction before applying the necessary processing.

library(tidyverse) 
library(gridExtra) 
library(ipumsr)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(sf)

map_dir<- "C:/Users/MISSONGO/Documents/AMSE Master 1/data visualization/MISSONGO_INGABIRE_NISABWE_SEYDINA"

Step 1 : Defining an extract request

  • API
set_ipums_api_key("59cba10d8a5da536fc06b59dc500e761eae6446692037290ac8a5989", save = TRUE)
  • Defining an Extract Map’s Information 
nhgis_ext_map <- define_extract_nhgis(
  description = "County shapefiles (2020)",
  shapefiles = "us_county_2020_tl2020"
)
  • Defining an Extract Pop’s Information 
nhgis_ext_pop <- define_extract_nhgis(
  description = "CW8: Persons by Sex by Race at county level",
  time_series_tables = tst_spec(
    "CW8",
    geog_levels = c("county"),
    years = c("2010")
  )
)

Step 2 : Submitting an Extract Request

nhgis_ext_submitted_map <- submit_extract(nhgis_ext_map)

nhgis_ext_submitted_pop <- submit_extract(nhgis_ext_pop)

Step 3 : Waiting for an Extract Request to Complete

nhgis_ext_complete_map <- wait_for_extract(nhgis_ext_submitted_map)

nhgis_ext_complete_pop <- wait_for_extract(nhgis_ext_submitted_pop)

Step 4: Download an extract

filepath_map <- download_extract(nhgis_ext_submitted_map,
                             download_dir = map_dir)

filepath_pop <- download_extract(nhgis_ext_submitted_pop,
                             download_dir = map_dir)

Step 5. Reading the data

  • Reading the data for Map 
shape_us <- read_ipums_sf(paste0(map_dir,"/nhgis0012_shape.zip"))

shape_us %>% 
  mutate(STATEFP = as.integer(STATEFP)) %>%
  filter(STATEFP < 57) %>% 
  filter(!(STATEFP %in% c(2,15))) ->
  shape_us

Preprocessing

  • Selection variables 
data <- data %>%
  select(GISJOIN, CW8AA2010, CW8AB2010, CW8AC2010, CW8AD2010,CW8AE2010,CW8AG2010, CW8AH2010, CW8AI2010, CW8AJ2010,CW8AK2010,  STATE) %>%
  mutate(pop_white = CW8AA2010 + CW8AG2010,
         pop_black = CW8AB2010 + CW8AH2010,
         pop_native = CW8AC2010 + CW8AI2010,
         pop_asian = CW8AD2010 + CW8AJ2010,
         pop_other = CW8AE2010 + CW8AK2010) %>%
  mutate(total_pop = pop_white + pop_black + pop_native + pop_asian + pop_other) %>%
  select(GISJOIN, STATE, pop_white, pop_black,pop_native,pop_asian, pop_other, total_pop)  ->
  data
  • Merge data 
final_data <- shape_us %>%
  left_join(data , by = "GISJOIN")

2. Task 1 : County population barplots

  • Select population of Los Angeles 
los_angeles_data <- final_data %>%
                    filter( NAME == "Los Angeles") %>%
                    pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("pop"), names_to="race", values_to = "population") %>%
                    mutate(race = str_sub(race, start=5)) %>%
                    mutate(race = factor(race, levels=c("white", "black", "asian", "native", "other"))) %>%
                    mutate(pop_share = round(population * 100 / sum(population), 2)) -> temp
  • Los Angeles population barplots 
p1 <- ggplot(temp, aes(y=race, x=population, fill=race)) +
      geom_col() +
      geom_text(aes(label = race, x=max(population) * .1), nudge_x = 0.3,
                color = "black", size = 3, fontface = "bold") + 
      labs(title= paste0("county: ", temp$NAME[1])) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5), legend.position = "none",axis.text.y = element_blank())    

p2 <- ggplot(temp, aes(y=race, x=pop_share, fill=race)) +
      geom_col() +
      geom_text(aes(label = pop_share, x=max(pop_share) * .1), nudge_x = 0.3,
                color = "black", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
      labs(x="population share (%)", y="", title="") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
      theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5), legend.position = "none",axis.text.y = element_blank())    

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1,p2, nrow=1)

3. Task 2: All counties

library(RColorBrewer)

breaks <- c(85, 7036, 13009, 20680, 32542, 54701, 131842, 9336275, Inf)

final_data$class_pop <- cut(final_data$total_pop, breaks =breaks,
                            include.lowest = TRUE, right = TRUE,
                            labels = c("85 to 7,036", "7,036 to 13,009", "13,009 to 20,680", "20,680 to 32,542", "32,542 to 54,701", "54,701 to 131,842", "131,842 to 9,336,275", "Missing"))

final_data$class_pop[is.na(final_data$class_pop)] <- "Missing"

colors <- brewer.pal(n = 7, name = "YlOrRd")
colors <- c(colors, "grey")

ggplot(data = final_data) +
geom_sf(aes(fill = factor(class_pop))) +
scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(colors,
                                    levels(factor(final_data$class_pop)))) +
labs(title = "Total Population of USA (2010)",
     fill = "Total Pop.") +
theme_minimal() +
theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 5.5),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.position = c(0.02, 0.2),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

3. Task 3: leaflet

transform_data <- st_transform(final_data, 4326)  # Transformation en WGS84 (EPSG:4326)
library(leaflet)

bks <- mapsf::mf_get_breaks(transform_data$total_pop, nbreaks = 7, breaks = "quantile")
pal_fun <- colorQuantile("YlOrRd", NULL, n = 7)

p_popup <- paste0("<strong>Total Population: </strong>", transform_data$total_pop,"<br>",
                      "<strong>County Id: </strong>", transform_data$GEOID,"<br>",
                      "<strong>County: </strong>", transform_data$NAME,"<br>",
                      "<strong>State: </strong>", transform_data$STATE)

leaflet(transform_data) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal_fun(total_pop),
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.8, smoothFactor = 0.5,
    popup = p_popup,
    group = "county",
  ) %>%
  addLegend("bottomright", 
                colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "YlOrRd"),
                values = transform_data$total_pop,
                labels = paste0("up to ", format(bks[-1], digits = 2)),
                title = 'Total Pop.')

us_states  <- sf::read_sf(paste0(paste0(map_dir, "/nhgis0012_shape"), "/US_county_2020.shp"))
us_states  <- us_states[sf::st_is_valid(us_states), ]
us_states %>% 
  mutate(STATEFP = as.integer(STATEFP)) %>%
  filter(STATEFP < 57) %>% 
  filter(!(STATEFP %in% c(2,15))) ->

us_states <- sf::st_transform(us_states, 4326)
us_states %>%
  sf::st_centroid() ->
  us_state_centroids
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title = "US County Population in 2010"),
  dashboardSidebar(
    sidebarMenu(
      menuItem("Filters", tabName = "filters", icon = icon("filter")),
      uiOutput("select_state"),
      uiOutput("select_county")
    )
  ),
  dashboardBody(
    fluidRow(
      box(leafletOutput("map", height = 250), width = 8)
    ),
    fluidRow(
      box(plotOutput("BarPlot", height = 250), width = 8)
    )

)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$select_state <- renderUI({
    req(transform_data)
    selectInput("select_state", "State:", choices = unique(transform_data$STATE))
  })

  output$select_county <- renderUI({
    req(input$select_state)
    selectInput("select_county", "County:", choices = transform_data$NAME[transform_data$STATE == input$select_state])
  })

output$BarPlot <- renderPlot({
   transform_data %>%
    select(STATE, NAME, starts_with("pop") ) %>%
    filter(NAME == input$select_county) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("pop"), names_to="race",
                 values_to = "population") %>%
    mutate(race = str_sub(race, start=5)) %>%
    mutate(race = factor(race, levels=c("white", "black", "asian",
                                        "native", "other"))) %>%
    mutate(pop_share = population * 100 / sum(population)) ->
    temp 

    p1 <- ggplot(temp, aes(y=race, x=population, fill=race)) +
     geom_col() +
     geom_text(aes(label = race, x=max(population) * .1), size=5,
               nudge_x = 0.3) + 
     labs(title= paste0("county: ", temp$NAME[1])) +
     theme_bw() +
     theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5), legend.position = "none",axis.text.y = element_blank())    

    p2 <- ggplot(temp, aes(y=race, x=pop_share, fill=race)) +
     geom_col() +
     labs(x="population share", y="", title="") +
     theme_bw() +
     theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5), legend.position = "none",axis.text.y = element_blank())    

    gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1,p2, nrow=1)

  })

  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    bks <- mapsf::mf_get_breaks(transform_data$total_pop, nbreaks = 7, breaks = "quantile")
    pal_fun <- colorQuantile("YlOrRd", NULL, n = 7)
    p_popup <- paste0("<strong>Total Population: </strong>", transform_data$total_pop,"<br>",
                      "<strong>County Id: </strong>", transform_data$GEOID,"<br>",
                      "<strong>County: </strong>", transform_data$NAME,"<br>",
                      "<strong>State: </strong>", transform_data$STATE)
    
    leaflet() %>%
      addPolygons(data=transform_data,
                  stroke = FALSE, 
                  fillColor = ~pal_fun(total_pop),
                  fillOpacity = 0.8, smoothFactor = 0.5,
                  popup = p_popup,
                  group = "county",
                  layerId = transform_data$GEOID) %>%
      addLegend("bottomright", 
                colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "YlOrRd"), 
                labels = paste0("up to ", format(bks[-1], digits = 2)),
                title = 'Total Pop.') %>%
      addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("state"),baseGroups = c("county")) 
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$map_shape_click, {
    output$text <- renderText({paste0("county id:",
                                      input$map_shape_click$id) })
    updateSelectInput(inputId = "select_county", 
          choices=transform_data$NAME[transform_data$GEOID == input$map_shape_click$id])
    updateSelectInput(inputId = "select_state", 
          choices=transform_data$STATE[transform_data$GEOID == input$map_shape_click$id])
  }) 
}

  observeEvent(input$map_shape_click, {
    selected_state <- transform_data$STATE[transform_data$GEOID == input$map_shape_click$id]
    selected_county <- transform_data$NAME[transform_data$GEOID == input$map_shape_click$id]
  
    output$text <- renderText({ paste0("County ID: ", input$map_shape_click$id) })
  
    updateSelectInput(session, "select_county", choices = transform_data$NAME[transform_data$STATE == selected_state], selected = selected_county)
  
    updateSelectInput(session, "select_state", selected = selected_state)
  })

shinyApp(ui, server)

Task 1.1 : Generating of the ERA5 data extract for Italy using the API of daily-hourly data starting in 2015

  • API and extraction 
## Get the Data

, key="6b209687-7f62-47b2-8829-0cd8f8a55f09")

  • Reading data and conversion

filename = DATADIR + "Italy_hourly_2015.nc"
ds = xr.open_dataset(filename)
da = ds['t2m']      # surface temp. at 2 meters
t2m_C = da - 273.15 # convert from Kelvin to Celsius

del ds, da

Task 1.2 : Aggregating and MAP

  • Aggregating local measures 

# aggregate hourly local data
year_month_day_mean = t2m_C.groupby(['time.year','time.month','time.day']).mean()

# aggregate local measures
weights = np.cos(np.deg2rad(year_month_day_mean))
weights = weights.fillna(0)
weights.name = "weights"
year_month_day_mean_weighted = year_month_day_mean.weighted(weights)
Italy_t2m = year_month_day_mean_weighted.mean(["longitude", "latitude"])
  • Italy’s Map 

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize = (16, 8), subplot_kw={'projection': ccrs.PlateCarree()})
im = plt.pcolormesh(year_month_day_mean.longitude, 
                    year_month_day_mean.latitude,
                    year_month_day_mean.sel(year=2022, month=8, day=3), 
                    cmap='RdBu_r', 
                    vmin=year_month_day_mean.sel(year=2022, month=8, day=3).min(), 
                    vmax=year_month_day_mean.sel(year=2022, month=8, day=3).max() ) 
ax.set_title('Mean temperatures on 03.08.2022', fontsize=16)
ax.gridlines(draw_labels=True, linewidth=1, color='gray', alpha=0.5, linestyle='--') 
ax.coastlines(color='black')
ax.set_extent([9, 18.5, 37, 46], crs=ccrs.PlateCarree()) 
cbar = plt.colorbar(im,fraction=0.05, pad=0.04)
cbar.set_label('temperature')

Task 1.3 : Downloading, Loading data and graph

  • Downloading data of Italy 
import pandas as pd

df = Italy_t2m.to_dataframe()
df = df.reset_index() 
df = df.drop(df[(df.month == 2) & (df.day > 28)].index)
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df[['year', 'month','day']])
df['week'] = df['date'].dt.isocalendar().week

temp = df.groupby(['year', 'week'])['t2m'].mean().reset_index()
temp.to_csv(DATADIR+"Italy_week_temperature.csv", index=False)
  • Loading data of Italy 
csv_file <- file.path(map_dir, "/Italy_week_temperature.csv")

data <- read.csv(csv_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  • Graph of Temperature Over the Years for Italy 
ggplot(data, aes(x = year + week / 52, y = t2m, group = year)) +

            fill = "gray", alpha = 0.2)+
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty(data$year)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "t2m") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

2. The mortality data

Task 2.1 : Downloading mortality data and selection

  • Downloading mortality data 
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akarlinsky/world_mortality/main/world_mortality.csv"
world_mort <- read_csv(url)
  • Selection Italy mortality data 
get_date <- function(year, week) {
  as.Date(paste(year, week, 1, sep = "-"), format = "%Y-%U-%u")
}
country <- "Italy"   ## iso3c == "ITA"

world_mort %>% 
   filter(iso3c == "ITA") %>%
   select(-c(iso3c,country_name,time_unit)) %>%
   rename(mortality=deaths, week=time) %>%
   mutate(start_date = get_date(week=week,year=year)) ->
   mortality

rm(world_mort)

head(mortality)

3. Simple time-series model of excess mortality

  • Estimating simple time-series model of excess mortality for the period before 2020-03-01 
library(lubridate)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

mortality_before_march <- mortality %>%
  filter(start_date < as.Date("2020-03-01"))

model <- lm(mortality ~ year + factor(week), data = mortality_before_march)

summer_2022 <- mortality %>%
  filter(start_date >= as.Date("2022-06-01") & start_date <= as.Date("2022-08-31"))

summer_2022$predicted_mortality <- predict(model, newdata = summer_2022)

summer_2022$excess_mortality <- summer_2022$mortality - summer_2022$predicted_mortality
  • Graph of Excess Deaths 
library(scales)

ggplot(summer_2022, aes(x = start_date, y = excess_mortality)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = "excess deaths")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("excess deaths" = "red")) +
  labs(title = "Italy: Excess Deaths",
       x = "date", y = "death count", color = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")

## [1] "Total number of excess deaths in Italy in summer of 2022 :  26773"

4. The mortality and temperature relationship

  • Merge data 
data <- data %>%
  left_join(mortality, by = c("year", "week"))
  • Bin scatter plot 
data$bin <- cut(data$t2m, breaks = quantile(data$t2m, probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE), include.lowest = TRUE)

means <- data %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(mean_t2m = mean(t2m, na.rm = TRUE), 
            mean_mortality = mean(mortality, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(data, aes(x = t2m, y = mortality)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = bin), method = "lm", color = "blue", se = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = means, aes(x = mean_t2m, y = mean_mortality), color = "blue", size = 3) +
  labs(x = "t2m", y = "mortality") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 1),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
